Subject: ISA
Title: Business Statistics
Description:
125 Introduction to Business Statistics (3)

This course provides an introduction to data, probability, sampling and its importance to analytical decision-making in business. Upon successful completion of this course, students will have the foundational skills necessary to summarize data, describe relationships among variables, and conduct one-sample and two-sample statistical inference. Note: Credit for graduation will not be given for more than one of STA 125, ISA 125, STA 261, STA 301, or STA 368. Prerequisites: MTH 102 or MTH 121 or MTH 125, MTH 122, MTH 141 or MTH 151; ACT Math Score of 22 or higher; SAT Math Score of 540 or higher; or Miami International Math Placement Test score of 8 or higher; or successful completion of MTH 025; or permission of department chair. Cross-listed with STA 125.
Attribute Description: Bus Course for Surcharge (BUS); TAG Course (TG)

Subject: ISA
Title: IT & Business Decision Making
Description:
211 Information Technology and Data Driven Decision Making in Business (3)

Introduction to the concepts of information systems and analytics used to support organizations for the non-business major. Focus is on the critical information technology and systems impacting the operations of organizations in the digital world. Additionally, how organizations use business analytics to make data-driven decisions will be covered.
Attribute Description: Bus Course for Surcharge (BUS)

Subject: ISA
Title: Business Analytics
Description:
225 Principles of Business Analytics (3)

Provides a continuation of the study of data and its importance to analytical decision-making in business. Topics include: probability and classification, data visualization, two or more population inference, predictive modeling with simple and multiple regression analysis, business forecasting, data-mining. Emphasis on computer implementation, analysis of real data, and communication of results. Prerequisite: (MTH 141 or MTH 151) and ISA/STA 125.
Attribute Description: Bus Course for Surcharge (BUS); TAG Course (TG)

Subject: ISA
Title: IT & Intelligent Enterprise
Description:
235 Information Technology and the Intelligent Enterprise (3)

This course prepares students for today’s tech and data driven business world through a focus on the strategic and transformational role of information technology and data. Topics include: challenges faced by business leaders and how information technology can help meet those challenges, technology driven innovation and disruptive technologies, information ethics, and the processes and policies needed to manage technical and digital assets. The course leverages the skills learned in the prerequisite course to further develop and demonstrate data driven business problem solving using tools such as spreadsheets, data visualization, and artificial intelligence. Prerequisite: CSE 148.
Additional Notes: Delivered via on campus face-to-face class meetings and asynchronous online learning
Attribute Description: Hybrid Asynchronous (HYBA); Bus Course for Surcharge (BUS); Top 25 (T25)

Subject: ISA
Title: Business Data Comm. & Security
Description:
301 Business Data Communications and Security (3) 

Introduces theory, concepts and applications of data communications technologies in a today’s business environment. It includes and introduction to personal, local and wide area network architectures as well as wired, wireless, and mobile technology standards employed in those architectures. The course also introduces the business issues related to network and data security and covers methodologies and technologies commonly employed to protect corporate data assets. Finally, the course explores emerging standards and other related management considerations such as cloud computing. Prerequisite: ISA 235.
Attribute Description: Bus Course for Surcharge (BUS)

Description:
612 Advanced Business Intelligence (3)

This course introduces business intelligence and its supporting corporate data infrastructure. Students will learn how to retrieve, clean, manipulate and model structured data for business intelligence. Several scenarios will be introduced to illustrate the variety of techniques that may be used in preparing data for analysis. Title: Communicating with Data
Description:
616 Communicating with Data (3)

Bridges the study of technical and computational tools to the audiences who need the results of this work. This course will span the entire process of developing a data analytic product from consultation with a client to implementing a solution to presenting the solution to the client. This course will address the fundamentals of effectively communicating with and about quantitative analyses. Topics include using data visualization to describe data; document descriptive, predictive, and prescriptive analytical methods for reproducibility; write professional white papers and technical reports; and ethical considerations related to writing and communication with data.

Subject: ISA
Title: Modeling & Optimization
Description:
634 Systems Modeling and Optimization (3)

This course offers a comprehensive exploration into several methods for designing and optimizing complex systems and complex decision processes. Students will learn the intricacies of creating mathematical programming models tailored to real-world scenarios, considering business metrics, resource constraints, and diverse decision-making contexts. Focus will also be put on modeling systems using networks, along with corresponding analysis tools rooted in graph theoretic methods. Throughout the course, students will gain insights into prescriptive analytics, network science, and complexity analysis, equipping them with skills applicable across various domains. Among others, practical examples from production management, supply chain dynamics, human resource allocation, financial modeling, and social network analysis will be used to demonstrate theoretical concepts and a wide range of applications.
